messages.subject: Error in validation of [0,1] probability parameter.
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to fit a model to some count data, which is essentially a logistic regression and I'm using a Poisson likelihood for the observed counts in caught and "not-caught" fish in an experimental trawl. So as a function of length, the probability of capture is `p[i]`, and the total number of fish caught is `lambda[i]`. This is all simple enough, however I'm having some issues with STAN. The model is:

data {
  int N;        // number of length classes
  int y1[N];    // number counted in codend
  int y2[N];    // number counted in cover
  real q[2];    // sampling fracions of (cover, codend)
  real len[N];  // length classes
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> l50;       // length of 50% retention probability
  real<lower=0> SR;        // 75% selection range
  real<lower=0> lambda[N]; // unknown total number of fish caught per lengthclass
}

transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0,upper=1> p[N];  // retention probability
  real theta[N];               // linear function of l50/SR/length
  
  for (i in 1:N) {
    theta[i] <- 2 * log(3) / SR * (len[i] - l50);  // alternate parametrization of beta[0] + beta[1] * len[i]
    p[i] <- inv_logit(theta[i]);
  }
}

model {
  l50 ~ lognormal(0, 10);
  SR ~ lognormal(0, 10);
  for (i in 1:N) {
    lambda[i] ~ lognormal(0, 100);
  }

  for (i in 1:N) {
    real lam[2];  // the two poisson process rates

    lam[1] <- q[1] * p[i] * lambda[i];
    lam[2] <- q[2] * (1 - p[i]) * lambda[i];

    y1[i] ~ poisson(lam[1]);
    y2[i] ~ poisson(lam[2]);
  }
}

The data are:
data.list <- 
structure(list(y1 = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 2L, 3L, 25L, 
47L, 65L, 57L, 28L, 16L, 5L, 1L, 0L), y2 = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 
0L, 2L, 0L, 8L, 6L, 34L, 82L, 62L, 37L, 12L, 3L, 0L, 0L, 0L), 
    q = c(0.585, 0.34), len = 6:23, N = 18L), .Names = c("y1", 
"y2", "q", "len", "N"))

For some reason, when I run this model it samples find until it produces values of `p = 1`, at which point I get the error message:
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
Invalid value of p: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: p[k0__] is nan:0, but must be greater than 0
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

Sometimes this only occurs a few times, but others it continues until I get the "Error: no acceptably small step size" message and sampling fails. When I print the values of `p`, before I get the above message, I am told `p = 1`, so I'm just confused as to why I'm getting an error telling me that `p` must be greater than 0! Surely the `inv_logit` function will only return values in [0,1]? (and I have also been sure to implicitly force p to be between 0 and 1. 

I have another more "well-behaved" data set which works 99% of the time, but still occasionally gets this error message; for the given data set it occurs almost every time I run it. I have the most recent version of RStan (14 Feb).

Thanks for any help.
- Tom

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error in validation of [0,1] probability parameter.
parts:
Sorry for the cryptic warning --- we need to do a better job of
saying exactly which parameter is causing problems.

I'm guessing the problem here (as indicating by your print) is
that you have values pushing up against boundaries. This will
cause numerical instabilities due to overflow or underflow in
the transforms.

The cryptic message comes about because the transform yields
a not-a-number value (NaN), and NaN is not > 0. The only
values getting transformed are the parameters --- everything
else happens inside code corresponding to the statements in
the transformed parameter or model blocks.

I'd suggest working on the log scale and vectorizing.

We have functions

log_inv_logit(u) = log(inv_logit(u))

and

log1m_inv_logit(u) = log(1 - inv_logit(u))

and a log-scale Poisson

poisson_log(y|alpha) =def= poisson(y|exp(alpha))

for just this reason.

Here's the rewritten model:

data {
int N; // number of length classes
int y1[N]; // number counted in codend
int y2[N]; // number counted in cover

vector[2] q; // sampling fracions of (cover, codend)
vector[N] len; // length classes

}

parameters {
real<lower=0> l50; // length of 50% retention probability
real<lower=0> SR; // 75% selection range

vector[N] log_lambda; // log of unknown total number of fish caught per lengthclass
}

transformed parameters {
vector[N] log_p; // log retention probability
vector[N] log1m_p; // log 1 - retention prob
vector[N] theta; // linear function of l50/SR/length

theta <- 2 * (log(3) / SR) * (len - l50);

parts:
We haven't quite published this policy yet, but we're going to be
asking people who want this level of advice to share their full models
and data so that we can show full before/after results and hopefully
start building up case studies that will be useful to future users.
You're implicitly our first guinea pig. And it helped that I was in
the middle of some really twisty C++ I wanted to procrastinate.

This is also a case where I'd be curious to see how well BUGS/JAGS
do in exploring the tails of the lambda fits in the broad prior model.

- Bob
